1.title: Copilot and Visual Calculations
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Copilot and Visual Calculations. It covers the exam area Visualize and analyze the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Create a narrative visual with Copilot. Use Copilot to create a new report page. Use Copilot to suggest content for a new report page. Create visual calculations by using dacks. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Visualize and analyze the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: What Copilot needs
1.text: What Copilot needs. Copilot in Power B I is an A I assistant that works only with the right capacity and settings. Check the requirements before you check anything else.

1.title: What Copilot needs, continued
1.text: What Copilot needs. The figure shows this: Requirements for Copilot in Power B I and the four skills of this module: narrative visual, new report page, suggested content and visual calculations.

1.title: What Copilot needs, continued
1.text: What Copilot needs. Capacity. A paid Fabric capacity of F two or higher, or a Premium capacity of P one or higher. Not enough. A trial capacity, or a Pro or P P U license alone. Tenant setting. The admin turns on "Users can use Copilot and other features powered by Azure Open A I". Region. The capacity must be in a supported region. Prompt limit. Up to ten thousand characters in one prompt. Delay. Copilot can take up to twenty-four hours to appear after you buy the capacity.

1.title: What Copilot needs, continued
1.text: What Copilot needs. Review every Copilot answer. Copilot is generated by A I and can be wrong, so you check the text, the visuals and the measures before you share the report. Exam tip: Copilot needs a paid capacity of F two or higher, or P one or higher. A trial, Pro alone or P P U alone is not enough. Also remember the tenant setting, a supported region and up to twenty-four hours of delay.

1.title: Narrative visual with Copilot
1.text: Narrative visual with Copilot. A narrative visual with Copilot writes a text summary of what the report shows. When you add the Narrative visual, it opens in Copilot mode. Scope. The whole report, chosen pages or selected visuals. Source. It reads the report visuals, not the semantic model directly. Editing. Change the text by typing a prompt, such as "make it shorter". Updating. It does not update on its own; the text stays until someone refreshes it. Older mode. Smart narrative, with dynamic values (up to four per visual and sixteen per page).

1.title: Narrative visual with Copilot, continued
1.text: Narrative visual with Copilot. The scope you choose decides which visuals Copilot reads. A summary of selected visuals describes only those visuals. Exam tip: The Copilot narrative reads the report visuals, not the model, and it does not refresh itself. The older smart narrative uses dynamic values that follow the data.

1.title: Create report pages and suggest content
1.text: Create report pages and suggest content. Copilot can build a new report page from the semantic model. In the Power B I service, open the report, choose Edit, then open Copilot. Suggest content for this report. What you do: Choose that prompt. Result: An outline of pages that you can pick from. Describe a page. What you do: Type what the page should show. Result: Copilot builds the page with visuals.

1.title: Create report pages and suggest content, continued
1.text: Create report pages and suggest content. After Copilot creates a page, you edit it by asking Copilot to add, change or delete visuals. Not supported: real-time streaming models, a live connection to Analysis Services, models where implicit measures are disabled, custom visuals, and formatting changes. Copilot builds the content; you still format the page and review it. Exam tip: Suggest content gives an outline of pages; describing a page gives one page. Copilot cannot change formatting, and it does not work with a live connection to Analysis Services.

1.title: Visual calculations
1.text: Visual calculations. A visual calculation is dacks that you write on a visual. It is stored in the visual, not in the model. It refers to the fields already in the visual, so no other visual can use it. running sum. Running total along the axis. moving average. Average over a moving window of rows. previous, next. The value of the previous or next row. first, last. The first or last value on the axis. range, lookup. A slice of rows, or a value you look up. collapse, expand, is at level. Work at a higher or lower level of the hierarchy.

1.title: Visual calculations, continued
1.text: Visual calculations. Two arguments steer the functions. Axis sets the direction in the visual, rows or columns. Reset sets where the calculation starts over: none, highest parent or lowest parent. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Visual calculations, continued
1.text: Visual calculations. Not supported: use relationship, related and related table; slicer visuals and some A I visuals; pinning to a dashboard; Publish to web; and filtering on the calculation itself. Exam tip: A visual calculation lives in the visual, not in the model, and cannot use related or use relationship. It cannot be pinned to a dashboard or published to the web.

1.title: Measure, column, visual calculation or calculation group
1.text: Measure, column, visual calculation or calculation group. Pick the calculation by where it must live and who must reuse it. A reusable value that reacts to filters in every visual. Use: Measure. Why: Calculated at query time in the model; nothing stored. A value per row to slice, sort, group or relate on. Use: Calculated column. Why: Stored in the model, calculated at refresh, uses memory. A running total, moving average or previous row in one visual. Use: Visual calculation. Why: Stored in the visual; the model does not change.

2.title: Measure, column, visual calculation or calculation group, continued
2.text: Measure, column, visual calculation or calculation group. One set of items, such as year to date, for many measures. Use: Calculation group. Why: Items use selected measure; explicit measures only. Creating a calculation group needs the setting Discourage implicit measures turned on. Exam tip: Many measures that need the same logic means a calculation group. One visual that needs a running total means a visual calculation. A value to slice by means a calculated column.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A company gives every analyst a Pro license, and its workspaces are on shared capacity. Analysts cannot find Copilot in the report editor. What is required? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A paid Fabric capacity of F two or higher. Copilot needs a paid Fabric capacity of F two or higher or a Premium capacity of P one or higher, and a trial, Pro or P P U alone is not enough.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. An author adds a Narrative visual with Copilot to a page. A viewer then selects a different region in a slicer. What happens to the narrative text? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: It stays as written until someone refreshes it. The Copilot narrative does not update on its own, so the text stays until it is refreshed.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A new report has a semantic model but no pages. The author wants Copilot to propose a set of pages before building any. Which prompt should the author choose? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Suggest content for this report. Suggest content for this report returns an outline of pages to pick from, while the others summarize or build one item.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. An author writes a visual calculation that returns a running total on a column chart. Where is the calculation stored, and who can reuse it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: In the visual, so no other visual can reuse it. A visual calculation is stored in the visual and is not part of the model, so other visuals cannot use it.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A team needs the same year-to-date and prior-year logic for twelve existing measures without writing twelve copies of each. Which feature should the team use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A calculation group with calculation items. A calculation group applies one set of calculation items to many explicit measures through selected measure.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. An author uses visual calculations in a report. Which of these actions is not supported? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Pinning the visual to a dashboard. Visuals that contain a visual calculation cannot be pinned to a dashboard, while running totals, moving averages and previous-row comparisons are supported.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which capacities allow Copilot? Answer: A paid Fabric capacity of F two or higher, or a Premium capacity of P one or higher. Question two. What are the prompt limit and the possible delay after you buy the capacity? Answer: ten thousand characters, and up to twenty-four hours. Question three. What are the two ways to start a Copilot report page? Answer: Suggest content for this report, or describe the page.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does a Copilot narrative visual read? Answer: The report visuals, not the semantic model directly. Question five. Which two arguments control a visual calculation function? Answer: Axis and Reset. Question six. What should you do with Copilot output before you share it? Answer: Review it, because it can be wrong.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Requirements: Paid F two or higher, or P one or higher; not trial, Pro or P P U alone. Limits: ten thousand-character prompt; up to twenty-four hours to appear. Narrative visual: Scope: report, pages or visuals; reads report visuals; edit by prompt; does not auto-update. Report page: Suggest content gives an outline; describe a page; edit by add, change, delete. Visual calculation: dacks stored in the visual; running sum, moving average, previous, next; Axis and Reset. Not supported: use relationship, related, related table, slicers, pin to dashboard, Publish to web. Which calculation: Measure: reusable; column: per row; visual calculation: one visual; calculation group: many measures. Review: Always review Copilot output before sharing.
